Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:1.english: With what are we dealing - [the case where] he enters to visit him.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:2.hebrew: אפילו יושב נמי - יהא מותר, שהרי נכסי חולה אין אסורין על המבקר, ומותר ליהנות משלו:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:2.english: Even sitting as well - It should be permitted, for the property of the ill person is not forbidden to the visitor, and it is permitted [for him] to benefit from his [property].

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:3.hebrew: אי בשנכסי כו' - ולהכי אינו יושב בישיבה, שלא יהנה משלו:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:3.english: If [it is a case] where the property [of the ill person is forbidden to the visitor], etc. - And therefore he does not sit down, so that he will not benefit from his [property].

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:4.hebrew: אפי' עומד לא - דהנאה היא לו שנהנה:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:4.english: Even standing, no - For it is a benefit to him that he derives benefit [from the ill person's property].

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:5.hebrew: ובמקום שנוטלין שכר על הישיבה - שכר שהולך לבקר את החולה ויושב עמו לצוותא, ומשכירין אותו:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:5.english: And in a place where they take payment for sitting - Payment [for] one who goes to visit the sick person and sits with him for companionship, and they hire him [for this].

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:6.hebrew: ואין נוטלין על העמידה - ולהכי אינו יושב, שאם היה יושב שם המבקר בחנם, מוותר היה לו שכרו ומהנהו אם לא יטול שכר. אבל עומד, הואיל ואין נוטלין שכר על העמידה, מותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:1:6.english: And one does not take [payment] for standing - And therefore he does not sit, for if the visitor were to sit there for free, he would be waiving his fee for him and benefiting him if he does not take payment. But [when] standing, since one does not take payment for standing, it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:1.english: Why [is this] fixed - That for this [sitting] they take payment, and not for that [standing].

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:10.hebrew: מאי פסקא - הא קמ"ל, אע"ג דאיכא דוכתא שנוטלין שכר, על הישיבה נוטלין אבל לא על העמידה, והיינו טעמא דבעמידה מותר אבל לא בישיבה. כדאמר ר"ש בן אליקים בשילהי פירקין גבי שביעית:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:10.english: Why [state this] categorically - This is what it teaches us: even though there are places where they take payment [for visiting the sick], for sitting they take [payment], but not for standing; and that is the reason that [visiting] while standing is permitted, but not while sitting. As Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said at the end of our chapter regarding the Sabbatical year.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:12.hebrew: שהרי עומד ואוכל - גזירה שמא ישהא בישיבה מרובה, והוי הנאת חולה. וא"ת: נגזור בעמידה כי היכי דגזרינן התם בעמידה? הא לא קשה: דאילו התם גזרי' בעמידה, אבל הכא, דלא מטיא ליה הנאה בעמידה, ליכא למיגזר שמא ירבה בעמידה; אבל לא בישיבה, שנוח לו לזה לישב — גזירה שמא ישהא בישיבה:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:12.english: For behold, he stands and eats - [Sitting is prohibited as] a decree lest he linger in prolonged sitting, and it constitutes a benefit of the sick person. And if you say: Let us decree [a prohibition] on standing, just as we decree there [in the case of Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim] on standing? This is not difficult: whereas there we decree on standing, here, where no benefit reaches him through standing, there is no reason to decree lest he prolong standing; but not [so] with sitting, since it is comfortable for this person to sit — [therefore it is] a decree lest he linger in sitting.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:2.hebrew: על העמידה לא בעי למשקל - דעראי הוא, דכך הוא בכל מקום. ולהכי עומד אבל לא יושב, דכיון דליכא שכר [על העמידה], לא מהני ליה כלל:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:2.english: For standing, one ought not to take - Because it is casual, as such is [the practice] in every place. And therefore he may stand, but not sit, because since there is no payment [for standing], he does not benefit him at all.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:3.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - לעולם בשנכסי מבקר אסורין על החולה, ואפילו במקום שאין נוטלין שכר על הישיבה. ודקאמרת אפי' יושב נמי — כדקאמר רבי שמעון בן אליקים לקמן (נדרים דף מב:) לענין שביעי':
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:3.english: And if you wish, say - Actually, [the Mishnah is speaking] where the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person, and even in a place where they do not take payment for sitting. And as for what you say, "Even one who sits should also [be permitted]" — [it is] as Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim says below (Nedarim 42b) regarding the Sabbatical year.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:4.hebrew: גזירה שמא ישהא בעמידה, הכא נמי שמא ישהא בישיבה - ושהייה דישיבה ודאי הנאה היא לחולה, ולהכי לא ישב עמו. ואי קשיא: אפילו עומד נמי לא — גזירה שמא ישהא בעמידה! הא לא קשיא, דהתם כיון דאכל מפירי דשדה, איכא למימר דלמא אגב דאכיל שהייה תמן אע"ג דקאי, והכא דלא אכל, משום הכי קאי: (לא מצאתי יותר מזה הלשון וזהו אמר ליה):
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:4.english: A decree lest he tarry while standing; here too, [a decree] lest he tarry while sitting - And tarrying while sitting is certainly a benefit to the sick person, and therefore he may not sit with him. And if you ask: Even [when] standing as well, let him not [be permitted to visit, due to] a decree lest he tarry while standing! This is not difficult, for there [in the case of Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim], since he eats from the fruits of the field, it is possible to say that perhaps while eating he will tarry there even though he is standing; whereas here, where he does not eat, for that reason he [may] stand. (I did not find more than this wording, and this is "he said to him.")

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:5.hebrew: אפילו יושב נמי - להוי מותר, דהא מבקר מותר בנכסי חולה:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:5.english: Even sitting as well - Let it be [permitted], for the visitor is permitted [to derive benefit] from the property of the ill person.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:6.english: Even standing - For he is forbidden from setting foot [there].

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:7.hebrew: לעולם בשנכסי מבקר אסורין על החולה - ומשום הכי עומד, אבל לא יושב, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:7.english: Actually, [it is speaking of a case] where the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person - And therefore he [may] stand, but not sit, as the Gemara explains:

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:8.hebrew: במקום שנוטלין שכר על הישיבה - דהיושב לפני החולה משתכר פורתא, משום דקעביד ליה צוותא בעלמא. והלכך בישיבה אסור, משום דקא מהני ליה ההוא אגרא דניתיב לאיניש אחרינא דיתיב קמיה:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:8.english: In a place where one takes payment for sitting - For one who sits before the sick person earns a little, because he provides him mere companionship. Therefore, sitting is prohibited, because he benefits him [with] that payment that he would [otherwise] give to another person who sits before him.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:9.hebrew: אבל בעמידה דמותר - משום דלא קמהני ליה ולא מידי, דהא לא עביד למיתב אגרא אעמידה:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:2:9.english: But while standing, which is permitted - Because he does not benefit him at all, for one is not accustomed to give payment for standing.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:3:1.hebrew: לעולם בשנכסי חולה אסורין על המבקר - וכשאין נוטלין שכר על העמידה, ולהכי מותר בעמידה, דהא לאו מן חיותיה נדר, כדאמר לקמן: כל המבקר את החולה גורם לו שיחיה, ואהכי מותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:3:1.english: Actually, [it is a case] where the property of the ill person is forbidden to the visitor - And [this is] when they do not take payment for standing, and therefore he is permitted [to visit] while standing, for he did not vow [to prohibit him] from [matters pertaining to] his life, as it says below: "Whoever visits the sick causes him to live," and therefore it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:3:2.hebrew: הא אפשר בעמידה - מבקרו בעמידה, דמהא לא אדריה, אבל בישיבה אדריה:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:3:2.english: Isn't it possible while standing - He visits him while standing, for regarding this he did not bind him by a vow, whereas regarding sitting he did bind him by a vow.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:4:1.english: If he became ill - The one who made the vow is permitted to visit him.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:4:2.english: [If] his son became ill - The one forbidden by the vow inquires of him in the marketplace about his son's affairs.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:4:3.hebrew: היינו דשני בין הוא לבנו - דאילו בשחלה הוא, מותר ליכנס לשם, דהא לא אדריה מן חיותיה. אבל כשחלה בנו, אינו נכנס לבקרו, דהא ליכא חיותא דמדיר:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:4:3.english: This is why [the baraita] distinguishes between him and his son - For whereas when he [himself] became ill, [the visitor] is permitted to enter there, since he did not vow [to forbid him] from [what pertains to] his existence; however, when his son became ill, he may not enter to visit him, since there is no [matter of] existence of the vower [involved].

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:5:1.hebrew: אלא לשמואל דאמר כו' מאי שנא הוא - דמותר, ומ"ש בנו דאסור? הא בעמידה ליכא הנאה כלל. אלא ודאי בנכסי חולה אסורין על המבקר מיירי וכדעולא, וקשיא לשמואל:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:5:1.english: However, according to Shmuel, who said, etc., what is different [about] him - [that he is] permitted, and what is different [about] his son that [he is] forbidden? Surely, in standing [to visit] there is no benefit at all. Rather, it is certainly speaking of [a case] where the property of the ill person is forbidden to the visitor, and [this is] like Ulla, and it is a difficulty for Shmuel.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:5:2.hebrew: אמר לך שמואל כו' וברייתא - מודינא דהכי הוא כדמוקי לה עולא, בשנכסי חולה אסורין על המבקר. מיהו בהא פליגנא עליה: דאיהו מוקי לה בעומד אבל לא ביושב, דהא אפשר בעמידה; ואנא אמינא דברייתא אפי' יושב שפיר דמי, דאמר דלא אדריה מן חיותיה — ל"ש עומד ול"ש יושב. ודיקא נמי, מדקתני סתמא "חלה הוא נכנס לבקרו", אפי' יושב:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:5:2.english: Shmuel could have said to you, etc., and the baraita - I concede that it is so as Ulla establishes it, [namely,] where the property of the ill person is forbidden to the visitor. However, in this [matter] I disagree with him: for he establishes it [as permitting visiting only while] standing, but not sitting, since it is possible [to visit] while standing; whereas I say that [in] the baraita, even sitting is proper, for he says that he did not prohibit him by vow from his sustenance, [so] there is no difference [whether he is] standing or sitting. And this is also indicated [by the wording], since it teaches without qualification, "if he fell ill, he may enter to visit him" — [meaning] even sitting.

Rashi on Nedarim 39a:6:1.hebrew: מאי פסקא - דמתני' בשנכסי מבקר אסורין על החולה:
Rashi on Nedarim 39a:6:1.english: Why [is it] categorical - that the Mishnah [refers to a case] where the visitor's property is forbidden to the sick person?

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:1:1.hebrew: אפי' עומד - דקא מתהני מדריסת הרגל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:1:1.english: Even [if he is] standing - For he derives benefit from setting foot [on the property].

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:1:2.hebrew: במקום שנוטלין שכר על הישיבה - לכך אסור לבקר בחנם, אבל בעמידה דאין נוטלין שכר עליה — מותר בחנם, דמצוה קעביד:
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:1:2.english: In a place where one takes payment for sitting - Therefore it is forbidden to visit for free, but [visiting] while standing — for which one does not take payment — is permitted for free, since he is performing a mitzvah.

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:2:1.hebrew: על העמידה לא בעי למשקל - כיון דמצוה הוא ויש לו לעשות בחנם; על הישיבה בעי למשקל, ואסור לעשות לו בחנם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:2:1.english: "For standing, he ought not to take [payment]" - Since it is a mitzvah and he should do [it] for free; [whereas] for sitting, he must take [payment], and it is forbidden to do [it] for him for free.

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:3:1.hebrew: דלא אדריה מחיותיה - כלומר, היינו טעמא דעומד, ואע"ג דאדריה מן ביתיה, לא היה דעתו לאסור עליו ביתו לבא כאן בשביל חיותו לבקרו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:3:1.english: Where he did not vow [to forbid] him from his sustenance - That is to say, this is the reason that he stands: even though he vowed [to forbid] him from his house, it was not his intention to forbid his house to him to come here for his sustenance, to visit him.

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:3:2.hebrew: אפשר בעמידה - והלכך בישיבה לא הוי חיותא, שאפשר למבקר להיות בעמידה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:3:2.english: [It is] possible while standing - And therefore, [visiting] while sitting is not [considered] a matter of survival, since it is possible for the visitor to be standing.

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:4:1.hebrew: חלה בנו שואלו בשוק - דאסור ליכנס בביתו [כיון שהדירו], וס"ד דברייתא מתפרשת כפי' דמתני':
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:4:1.english: "If his son became ill, he inquires about him in the marketplace" - For he is forbidden to enter his house [since he vowed against him], and [the Gemara] initially assumed that the baraita is explained according to the explanation of the Mishnah:

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:4:2.hebrew: בשלמא לעולא ניחא - דשרי לבקרו הוא, ולבנו אסור — אחיותיה דבנו אדרה. אלא לשמואל, כי היכי דלאביו שרי בעמידה, ה"נ בנו מותר בעמידה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:4:2.english: "Granted, according to Ulla, it is well" - For it is permitted to visit him, whereas for his son it is forbidden — [since] regarding his son's existence he did vow [to forbid it]. But according to Shmuel, just as for his father it is permitted [to visit] while standing, so too [for] his son it is permitted while standing.

Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:6:1.hebrew: פסקת - הדבר [דמתני' בשנכסי] מבקר אסור, וברייתא כשחולה אסור — הוה ליה לשנות התנא הברייתא בענין דמתניתין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 39a:6:1.english: Pasakta [You decided] - the matter, that the Mishnah [refers to] when the visitor's property is forbidden [to the ill person], and the Baraita [refers to] when the ill person's [property] is forbidden [to the visitor] — the Tanna should have taught the Baraita in the [same] manner as the Mishnah.
